title: Household demand model for India and Pakistan alternative-protein retail value

decisions.decision: Standalone reproducible model and paper; the D1 table is one output.
Headline: retail value, US dollars, constant 2025 prices, market exchange rates. Also report volume (tonnes) and share of household protein spending. The model works in shares.
Household model covers plant-based meat and dairy alternatives. Egg and fermentation products are carried from the proxy as a labelled residual so totals match GFI scope.
Report beside the GFI-anchored proxy and discuss the gap.
The US is the comparison and calibration market: BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey microdata plus GFI/SPINS 2025 retail sales of $7.9 billion. Nothing in the US is invented.
Code lives in the public library at `sentient-futures-research/research/household-demand/`. `future-research/` stays the supply benchmark; its AGENTS.md role is unchanged.

One price snapshot of public product pages, collected once: India Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Kolkata, Pune, one tier-2 city; Pakistan Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad. Price per kg product and per kg protein.
Validation: leave-one-state-out holdout is primary. A time comparison against HCES 2011-12 and 2022-23 is secondary, after the author registers at microdata.gov.in.

Vegetarian households are calibrated to NFHS-5 never-eat rates by state, religion and caste, after the author registers with the DHS Program. Until then, a 7-day zero-purchase rule runs as a labelled diagnostic.
Elicitation uses Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT Astra (`gpt-6-astra`) only, with tools already on this machine. No paid gateway.
Drivers: IMF and UN official projections with low, mid and high bands, plus an AI cost-decline path and a price-parity scenario.
Acceptance: protocol registered before any estimate; Codex recomputes every number; the team agrees the method before D1; human scholarly review stays pending.
Intent-to-purchase conversion from the US, adjusted by each country's price gap through measured price elasticity.
Adoption over time: Bass diffusion fitted to South Asian analog products fixed in the protocol; the US plant-based sales path is a stress test.
Soya chunks (HCES item 152) are an analog for price, diffusion and substitution, excluded from the market figure.

Plant-based meat substitutes for chicken in meat-eating households and competes with paneer, soya chunks and pulses in vegetarian households. Dairy alternatives substitute for liquid milk. Cross-price elasticities come from the microdata.
Halal certification is assumed met for any product sold in Pakistan. No scenario switch.
Design-based variance where strata are resolved; PSU-clustered bootstrap elsewhere, flagged.
India runs on real HCES microdata labelled diagnostic until baseline acceptance. Invented values only where data are absent: Pakistan unresolved strata and plant-based prices before the snapshot.
Publish summarised prices or publicly available data only; respect robots.txt; raw page captures stay local.
One joint Monte Carlo over elasticities, conversion, diffusion and driver bands; Sobol first-order and total indices.
Invented values carry a `SYNTHETIC` flag, live in their own folder, and a CI check blocks them from the claim ledger, reports and D1.
Run Anna's exact US questionnaire on the same two models as a labelled calibration; tell Anna before reporting it.
Chicken prices come from HCES and HIES unit values by state or province. The scraped chicken rows are not used.
Questionnaire asks for both the headline forecast and model inputs; compare the panel headline with the model computed from panel inputs.
India and Pakistan headline questions are marked unresolvable now, plus resolvable proxy questions: Comtrade HS 210610 imports, snapshot product counts, a republished GFI India estimate.

Replace the cultivated and fermentation category question with a plant-based meat versus dairy-alternative split, plus a yes/no question on the year of first approved cultivated-meat sale (FSSAI; Pakistan equivalent).
Each country gets a public evidence pack shaped like the US one, excluding this project's own estimates.
10 fresh-context runs per model per region; report the median and the 10th to 90th percentile spread across runs.
Web search allowed; sources logged; runs citing `github.com/Omarzaf`, `pakistan-india-protein.vercel.app` or `cultivated-chicken-halal.vercel.app` are discarded and rerun.

forecast.currency_rule: INR and PKR deflated to 2025 with official CPI, then converted at market exchange rates

status_flags.guard_rule: Whole uppercase word SYNTHETIC on any line of a text file under a surface is a hit; a missing surface fails (ruling R1).

analogs.rule: Task 7 gathers each candidate series with source, locator and years. A candidate with no public annual time series of at least 5 points is dropped and recorded with the reason. If no candidate survives for a country, the main diffusion uses priors.bass_fallback and the US path stays the stress test (ruling R8).

candidates.series_needed: annual packaged (pouch, UHT or carton) liquid milk volume or household penetration, national, at least 5 consecutive years
candidate_sources: India: annual reports of national dairy cooperatives and listed dairies, or NDDB statistics, if they split packaged from loose milk
Pakistan: annual reports of listed UHT milk processors, or Pakistan Economic Survey dairy tables, if they split packaged from loose milk

candidates.role: analog for price, diffusion and substitution; excluded from the market figure (decision 15)
candidates.series_needed: per capita quantity and share of households reporting purchase, by NSS consumption round
candidate_sources: NSS 68th round 2011-12, HCES 2022-23 and HCES 2023-24 item 152 aggregates (2011-12 and 2022-23 need the author's microdata.gov.in registration)

candidates.series_needed: annual branded ready-to-cook or processed chicken sales value or volume, national, at least 5 consecutive years
candidate_sources: India: annual reports of listed poultry processors with a processed or ready-to-cook segment
Pakistan: public filings or trade statistics for branded frozen chicken, if any exist

us_stress_test.series: GFI US plant-based retail sales (SPINS), 2018 to 2025
us_stress_test.role: stress test only (decision 14); main results use the analog diffusion
us_stress_test.values_status: Task 7 captures yearly values with locators

bass_fallback.source: Sultan, Farley and Lehmann (1990), A Meta-Analysis of Applications of Diffusion Models, Journal of Marketing Research 27(1), 70 to 77
bass_fallback.verification: Citation verified 18 October 2026. p and q confirmed through a citing paper; the original article's tables were not reached.
bass_fallback.use: main diffusion only if no analog survives (ruling R8)

India.note: first national plant-based meat retail launches (ruling R9); no source found

priors.halal: Certification assumed met for any product sold in Pakistan; no scenario switch (decision 17).

primary.citation: Bryant, C., Szejda, K., Parekh, N., Deshpande, V. and Tse, B. (2019). A Survey of Consumer Perceptions of Plant-Based and Clean Meat in the USA, India, and China. Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems 3, article 11.

corrigendum.effect: Corrects the spelling of Deshpande and the clean meat purchase-likelihood figures. No plant-based meat figure changes.

primary.instrument: One online questionnaire, CINT panel. Purchase likelihood on a 5-point Likert scale from 1 (not at all likely) to 5 (extremely likely). Locator: Materials and Methods, Materials.
primary.sample_caveat: India sample disproportionately urban, high income and well educated (Abstract).

locators.shares: Results, Descriptive Statistics, Acceptance, second paragraph
locators.means: Table 1, ANOVA results showing omnibus results and pairwise comparisons, row Likelihood of purchasing plant-based meat

primary.intent_share_definition: Share answering 4 or 5 (very or extremely likely) to plant-based meat purchase likelihood. USA 0.329, India 0.628.

missing.India_urban_meat_eater_subset_note: The article reports no urban meat-eater breakdown. Missing.
missing.dairy_alternative_intent_note: The article covers plant-based and clean meat only. Missing.

Pakistan.rule: The India intent range is transferred. The Pakistan household-model result is a scenario labelled CONDITIONAL_TRANSFER and never enters claims as a headline (ruling R9).

us_calibration.inputs: BLS CE public-use microdata (after author approval), GFI/SPINS 2025 retail sales 7.9e9 USD, GFI 2025 US household penetration (captured in Task 6 with locator), intent_sources.primary USA intent share
us_calibration.assumption: All US buyers sit in the addressable segment (ruling R7). Overstates conversion if buyers sit outside it.
us_calibration.addressable_rule: urban, buys meat, buys prepared or packaged food (Task 5), applied to the US, India and Pakistan alike

household_tables.India_mpce: HCES 2023-24 monthly per capita consumption expenditure, mpce_inr; mpce_local = mpce_inr; currency INR
household_tables.Pakistan_mpce: Total monthly household consumption expenditure from HIES 2024-25 divided by household size: use the PBS household total if a file holds it, else sum the consumption sections; document the source. mpce_pkr; mpce_local = mpce_pkr; currency PKR (ruling R4).
household_tables.cluster: psu (India: FSU identifier from level_01; Pakistan: prcode), stratum and stratum_status; India always RESOLVED (ruling R2)
household_tables.Pakistan_geography: state = province code, sector = region (1 rural, 2 urban); province and region kept (ruling R3)

validation.outcome: weighted per capita monthly spending on animal protein by state

statistics.mae: mean absolute error across held-out states
statistics.median_ape: median absolute percentage error across held-out states
statistics.coverage_80: share of states whose observed value falls inside the predicted 10th to 90th percentile

validation.secondary: time comparison against HCES 2011-12 and 2022-23 after the author registers at microdata.gov.in

elicitation.summary: median and 10th to 90th percentile spread across runs
